at_least_five_manifestations_present.assessment: The chart documents fever, conjunctivitis (bilateral not specified but likely), strawberry tongue, changes in extremities (inflammation and desquamation), and cervical lymphadenopathy—all five were present, so at least five manifestations are confirmed.
at_least_five_manifestations_present.evidence: fever; conjunctivitis; strawberry tongue; inflammation of the hands and feet, desquamation; cervical lymphadenopathy

fever_duration_value_recorded_now_in_day.assessment: The patient is reported to have had 5 days of high fever.

__THRESH__::fever_duration_value_recorde.assessment: The patient’s fever duration is documented as 5 days, meeting the ≥5 days threshold.

manifestation_1_present.assessment: Fever persisting 5 days is explicitly documented.

manifestation_2_present.assessment: Conjunctivitis is reported, which typically refers to bilateral conjunctival congestion in the clinical context of Kawasaki Disease.

manifestation_3_present.assessment: Strawberry tongue and oral mucosal changes are documented.

manifestation_4_present.assessment: Polymorphous exanthema (rash) is not specifically mentioned; the chart is silent on rash.

manifestation_5_present.assessment: Inflammation and desquamation of hands and feet are noted, directly supporting peripheral extremity changes.
manifestation_5_present.evidence: inflammation of the hands and feet, desquamation of the skin of the fingers and toes

manifestation_6_present.assessment: Cervical lymphadenopathy is recorded, with node size noted.
manifestation_6_present.evidence: cervical lymphadenopathy with the smallest node at 1.5 cm

manifestations_count.assessment: The chart documents 5 of the 6 specified manifestations: (1) fever ≥5 days, (2) conjunctivitis, (3) strawberry tongue (oral cavity changes), (4) changes of peripheral extremities (inflammation, desquamation), (5) acute cervical lymphadenopathy. No explicit mention of polymorphous exanthema (rash).
manifestations_count.evidence: Fever for 5 days; conjunctivitis; strawberry tongue; inflammation of hands/feet, desquamation; cervical lymphadenopathy (1.5 cm). No mention of rash.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_acute_febrile_m.assessment: The patient has compatible clinical findings (prolonged fever, conjunctivitis, oral changes, extremity changes, lymphadenopathy) and coronary artery involvement, meeting classic criteria for acute Kawasaki disease.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_acute_febrile_m.evidence: Fever for 5 days, conjunctivitis, strawberry tongue, extremity inflammation/desquamation, cervical lymphadenopathy, plus coronary artery dilation on echo.

patient_has_finding_of_cervical_lymphade.assessment: Cervical lymphadenopathy is explicitly documented on exam.
patient_has_finding_of_cervical_lymphade.evidence: Cervical lymphadenopathy with the smallest node at 1.5 cm.

patient_has_finding_of_cervical_lymphade.assessment: The presentation is acute (5 days of fever and findings); thus, lymphadenopathy is acute.
patient_has_finding_of_cervical_lymphade.evidence: Cervical lymphadenopathy described in patient presenting with 5 days of fever (acute presentation).

patient_has_finding_of_cervical_lymphade.assessment: No mention of purulence; standard for Kawasaki lymphadenopathy is nonpurulent. Absence of purulent description supports assignment.
patient_has_finding_of_cervical_lymphade.evidence: Cervical lymphadenopathy with the smallest node at 1.5 cm; no indication of purulent process.

patient_has_finding_of_congestion_of_thr.assessment: No mention of pharyngeal or throat congestion or erythema.

patient_has_finding_of_passive_conjuncti.assessment: Conjunctivitis is explicitly documented on exam, compatible with conjunctival congestion.
Kawasaki conjunctivitis is typically bilateral, and no unilateral finding is noted; standard clinical inference in this context is bilateral.
patient_has_finding_of_passive_conjuncti.evidence: Physical exam reveals conjunctivitis (in the setting of suspected Kawasaki disease, this is inferred bilateral unless specified otherwise).

patient_has_finding_of_disease_of_mouth_.assessment: Strawberry tongue is a classic mucosal change of the mouth in Kawasaki disease.

patient_has_finding_of_disease_of_periph.assessment: The note describes 'inflammation of the hands and feet, desquamation of the skin of the fingers and toes,' which are changes affecting the peripheral extremities.
patient_has_finding_of_disease_of_periph.evidence: inflammation of the hands and feet, desquamation of the skin of the fingers and toes

patient_has_finding_of_disorder_of_lip_n.assessment: The note states the patient has a 'strawberry tongue,' which meets the criterion of changes involving the oral cavity; changes of the lips are not explicitly described, but the oral involvement is present.
patient_has_finding_of_disorder_of_lip_n.evidence: strawberry tongue (oral involvement), silent on changes of lips: defer to visit

patient_has_finding_of_edema_now.assessment: The patient is noted to have 'inflammation of the hands and feet,' but no term for 'edema' is used; as edema is a specific manifestation, and the chart is silent on its presence, default to NULL.

patient_has_finding_of_edema_now@@indura.assessment: No mention of indurative (firm) edema is documented in the chart.

patient_has_finding_of_edema_now@@initia.assessment: There is no staging or timing provided regarding the initial stage of illness or related edema.

patient_has_finding_of_eruption_now.assessment: The note reports 'desquamation of the skin of the fingers and toes', but this refers to peeling and not an active eruption (rash); there is no mention of a current eruption or exanthema.

patient_has_finding_of_eruption_now@@pol.assessment: There is no mention of a polymorphous (variable) rash or eruption in the chart.

patient_has_finding_of_fever_now.assessment: The patient is described as having 5 days of high fever on presentation to the emergency department, indicating fever is present at time of presentation.

patient_has_finding_of_fever_subsided_be.assessment: There is no indication that the patient's fever has subsided before the 5th day or in response to therapy.

patient_has_finding_of_palmar_erythema_n.assessment: The note reports 'inflammation of the hands and feet,' which may suggest erythema but does not explicitly mention palmar erythema; default to NULL.

patient_has_finding_of_peeling_of_skin_n.assessment: The chart explicitly states 'desquamation of the skin of the fingers and toes', supporting that the patient currently has skin peeling.
patient_has_finding_of_peeling_of_skin_n.evidence: desquamation of the skin of the fingers and toes

patient_has_finding_of_peeling_of_skin_n.assessment: While desquamation is noted, the chart does not specify the timing/stage (acute vs convalescent), so default to NULL.
The chart notes desquamation of 'the skin of the fingers and toes', which encompasses the fingertips; clinical inference supports that the peeling is from the fingertips.
patient_has_finding_of_peeling_of_skin_n.evidence: desquamation of the skin of the fingers and toes

patient_has_finding_of_reddening_of_sole.assessment: The chart mentions 'inflammation of the hands and feet', which may include redness but does not specifically confirm reddening of the soles, so defer to visit.

patient_has_finding_of_strawberry_tongue.assessment: The chart explicitly documents 'strawberry tongue', confirming this clinical finding.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_acute_febrile_m.assessment: The patient currently exhibits fever >5 days, conjunctivitis, strawberry tongue, inflammation/desquamation of extremities, cervical lymphadenopathy, and coronary artery involvement—matching the acute phase of Kawasaki disease as defined by the trial.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_acute_febrile_m.evidence: Physical exam reveals conjunctivitis, strawberry tongue, inflammation of the hands and feet, desquamation of the skin of the fingers and toes, and cervical lymphadenopathy; echocardiogram shows moderate dilation of the coronary arteries with possible coronary artery aneurysm.
